صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً , in the Kur [xcviii. 2], signifies Writings cleansed from impurities and falsehood. (TA.) ―
-b2- And أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ, in the same [ii. 23], Wives purified from the pollution of the menstrual discharge and the other natural evacuations. (O, TA.) ―
-b3- And لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا المُطَهَّرُونَ, in the same [lvi. 78], is said by some to mean, (assumed tropical:) None shall attain to the knowledge of its true meanings except those who have purified themselves from the filth of corrupt conduct, and ignorances, and acts of disobedience. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
